title: 2023 HMMT November Guts Problem 6
statement: There are five people in a room. They each simultaneously pick two of the other people in the room independently and uniformly at random and point at them. Compute the probability that there exists a group of three people such that each of them is pointing at the other two in the group.

solutions.text:
The desired probability is the number of ways to pick the two isolated people times the probability that the remaining three point at each other. So,

\[P=\binom{5}{2} \cdot\left(\frac{\binom{2}{2}}{\binom{4}{2}}\right)^{3}=10 \cdot\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{3}=\frac{5}{108}\]

is the desired probability.
